newsitem.title: USA: NYC may use business clout to protect Christians.
newsitem.headline: NYC may use business clout to protect Christians.

text.p: New York City Council Speaker Peter Vallone introduced legislation Wednesday to restrict the city from dealing with companies that do business in 15 countries that allegedly persecute Christians.

"My legislature would divest city funds from banks that operate in these countries and prohibit the city from contracting with businesses that have a presence in those countries," Vallone told reporters at City Hall.
The legislation was aimed at China, Sudan, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Nigeria, Turkey, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Iraq, Morocco, Laos, and Vietnam.

Vallone, a Democrat, did not cite any data on how many companies would be affected by his proposal or give any indication of how much money was being invested in these countries by businesses that deal with New York City.

"I can assure you that there will be many objections to the bill," Vallone said, indicating that he expects to find out the level of investments once companies testify before the Council on the measure. When hearings might be held was not immediately known.

New York City has taken similar steps against companies that did business in South Africa and Northern Ireland and the Council on Wednesday also approved a bill restricting dealings with companies that are active in Burma. The City Council put on hold a proposal to require the city's pensions to divest themselves of Swiss banks' stocks after the Swiss government in February created a fund for Holocaust victims.

"There was a tirade of protests when we introduced legislation regarding South Africa," Vallone recalled. He added: "The city has enormous economic might overseas and we should use it whenever necessary to end human injustice."
